result.title: PRISM: Profiling and Representation of Individual Stereotypical Motion
result.summary: An anatomical pose provides interpretable joint structure, but no fixed set of physical landmarks can fully specify a person's movement. We introduce PRISM, a complementary representation that characterizes repetitive movement using tracked masks and dense optical flow. Torso-relative flow measures intensity, frame-wise mask variation measures spatial extent, signed-flow recurrence estimates frequency, and persistent sliding-window geometry describes the rhythmicity of the movement. Across 1,890 synthetic conditions, the measurements recover controlled speed, amplitude, and frequency while exposing observation limits. An idealized hand-motion experiment demonstrates variation omitted by identical exact COCO-17 trajectories; controlled corruption experiments separately examine measurement sensitivity. Audits of two pose methods on the same data cohort and 36,930 external skeleton clips document incomplete observation and dependence on processing choices. In 1,404 annotated complex stereotypical motor movement bouts from six autistic participants, total flow converges with pose motion, while matched-coordinate examples and repeated-session profiles show differences in intensity, extent, frequency, and rhythmicity within behavior labels. A separate VLM comparison evaluates quantitative frequency estimation, and a profile-conditioned decoder links the measurements to illustrative skeletal movements. PRISM connects numerical profiles to visible examples, providing an interpretable way to compare how the same behavior is expressed beyond its label or event count.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 PRISM，用跟踪掩码与稠密光流构建重复性运动的可解释剖面量（强度、空间范围、频率、节律），在合成条件、外部骨架片段与自闭症参与者刻板运动数据上核验其测量行为，并与 VLM 的频率估计作对比。
AI.relevance_reason: 该文指出固定姿态关键点无法完整刻画运动、需补充稠密视觉证据，可能为 LVR 中「任务必要视觉细节是否保留在表示中」的表示设计与评测提供线索，但属临床行为视频分析，与推理任务的迁移性尚待核查。
